questions.q: Who publishes and maintains the Zero Trust Maturity Model referenced in this lesson?
options: The SABSA Institute
NIST's Computer Security Division
The Open Group
CISA, the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency
questions.explain: CISA, the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, publishes and maintains the Zero Trust Maturity Model, now at version 2.0.

questions.q: What are the five pillars of CISA's ZTMM?
options: Prevention, Detection, Response, Recovery, Governance
Identity, Devices, Networks, Applications & Workloads, Data
Confidentiality, Integrity, Availability, Authenticity, Accountability
Business, Data, Application, Technology, Security
questions.explain: ZTMM v2.0 organizes zero trust around five pillars: Identity, Devices, Networks, Applications & Workloads, and Data, cut across by three cross-cutting capabilities.

questions.q: What are the four maturity stages a pillar is scored against in ZTMM?
options: Planned, In Progress, Complete, Verified
Low, Medium, High, Critical
Traditional, Initial, Advanced, Optimal
Draft, Reviewed, Approved, Retired
questions.explain: Each pillar moves through four stages — Traditional, Initial, Advanced, and Optimal — progressing from manual, perimeter-based controls toward automated, continuously verified ones.

questions.q: How does this lesson say an enterprise architect should use ZTMM, as distinct from how it was used in the security engineering course?
options: As a vendor product comparison chart for selecting zero trust tooling
As a gap-analysis artifact comparing current and target maturity, pillar by pillar, to inform planning and sequencing rather than prescribing specific controls
As a replacement for the SABSA Business Attributes Profile in every engagement
As a compliance certificate that satisfies SOC 2 and ISO 27001 requirements automatically
questions.explain: Used as an architecture input, a ZTMM assessment is a gap-analysis deliverable — current stage versus target stage per pillar — that feeds planning and sequencing decisions, not a list of controls to deploy.

questions.q: Which TOGAF ADM phases does a ZTMM maturity baseline most directly feed, according to this lesson?
options: Phase D (Technology Architecture) for target-state design, and Phases E/F (Opportunities & Solutions, Migration Planning) for sequencing gaps into work packages
Only the Preliminary phase, before any architecture work begins
Phase A (Architecture Vision) exclusively, with no further role later in the ADM
Phase H (Architecture Change Management) only, once implementation is already complete
questions.explain: A pillar-by-pillar maturity score lines up with Phase D's technology building blocks, and the gaps between current and target stage become candidate work packages sequenced in Phases E and F.
